title: Thirteen people, twelve places
summary: Two classes this term have had one more person on the register than the room has places, and both had been showing as full for days beforehand. A separate report has a cancelled place never coming back. Nothing is in the logs for any of it.

checkpoints.title: A booking takes a place and a cancellation gives it back
checkpoints.hint: A booking writes one row in state `booked` and takes one place off the class. A cancellation puts that row in state `cancelled` and gives the place back, and cancelling the same booking twice gives back one place rather than two. `NotFound` for a class or a booking that is not there, `NotAMember` and `ClassFull` before anything is written.

checkpoints.title: Two bookings taken at the same moment both come off the places left
checkpoints.hint: `places_left` is read before the membership check and written after it, and the other channel booked and committed in between. The number written down was worked out in this process from a row that has since moved on, and the transaction around the writes does not contradict it: a transaction promises all-or-nothing, not that a row you read is still what you read. Let the database do the arithmetic on the row it is writing, with `SET places_left = places_left - 1`.

checkpoints.title: The last place in a class goes to one person, and the other is refused
checkpoints.hint: Deciding there is a place and taking it are two separate steps here, so both callers can decide yes and both can write. Make the write the decision: put the condition in the statement, `WHERE id = ? AND places_left > 0`, and read `changes` off the result. Nought rows changed is the caller who has to be told the class is full, and throwing inside `db.transaction(fn)` is what takes their booking row back out.

checkpoints.title: A cancellation taken during a booking keeps the place it gave back
checkpoints.hint: It is not only about two bookings. Anything that commits between a read and the write built on it is lost the same way, and a lost cancellation is lost in silence: the place comes back and then goes again. `places_left` has to equal `capacity` minus the bookings still in state `booked` whatever landed in between, which it does once every write moves the count relative to itself rather than to a number from earlier.
